mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three months signals a restrictive monetary stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which pressure corporate margins and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE exceeds 6.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary tightening, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to lower unemployment, which signals weak wage growth and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized growth in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 5% for two consecutive quarters signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced consumer spending, which depresses corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 5% annualized for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered quarters, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.
